title: Special Array II
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> group: n entries → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input nums, returned vector<bool> ans
approach: A subarray is special iff no adjacent pair inside it has equal parity. Precompute a `group` id for each index: start a new group exactly at each index `i` where `nums[i]` and `nums[i-1]` share parity. Then a query `[l, r]` is special iff `group[l] == group[r]`, because equal group ids mean no parity-breaking boundary lies between them. This gives O(n + q) total time.
hints: With up to 10^5 queries each spanning up to 10^5 elements, what single precomputed label per index would let you answer any range query in O(1)?
Assign each index a group id; a new group starts exactly where two adjacent elements share parity. For nums = [4,3,1,6], the groups are [0,0,1,1] because 3 and 1 are both odd.

**Single element** - n = 1, the only possible query is a single index
`Input: nums = [5], queries = [[0,0]]` → `Expected: [true]`
⚠️ Bug: returning `l != r` as a precondition for `true` → returns `[false]`

**All same parity** - every adjacent pair breaks the special property
`Input: nums = [2,4,6,8], queries = [[0,3],[1,2]]` → `Expected: [false,false]`
⚠️ Bug: comparing `group[l] < group[r]` instead of `==` → returns `[true,true]`

**Boundary indices** - query touches the first or last element
`Input: nums = [3,4,1,2,6], queries = [[0,3],[4,4]]` → `Expected: [true,true]`
⚠️ Bug: starting the loop at `i = 0` and reading `nums[i-1]` → out-of-bounds read, corrupts `group[0]`

**Break at the query boundary** - the breaking pair sits just outside the queried range
`Input: nums = [3,4,1,2,6], queries = [[0,3]]` → `Expected: [true]`
⚠️ Bug: incrementing the group id when parities differ (inverted condition) → groups become `[0,1,2,3,3]`, returns `[false]`

followUps.q: For each query, also return the number of maximal special subarrays fully contained in nums[l..r].
followUps.a: Build a prefix count `pref[i]` = number of group starts in [0..i]. A new group starts at i when i==0 or parities of i and i-1 match. Answer = pref[r] - pref[l] + 1. TC O(n+q), SC O(n).

followUps.q: Support point updates that change an element's value (and possibly its parity), then answer queries online.
followUps.a: Replace the static group array with a segment tree storing, per segment, whether it is internally special and the parity of its endpoints; merging two children checks the boundary pair. Each update and query is O(log n). TC O((n+q) log n), SC O(n).

followUps.q: "Special" now means adjacent elements differ by exactly k (not parity). Answer the same queries.
followUps.a: The group structure is identical - start a new group wherever |nums[i]-nums[i-1]| != k. Precompute groups once, then answer each query by comparing group ids. TC O(n+q), SC O(n).
